primitives.name: Score-Level Fusion
primitives.verbatim_quote: The fusion gate and calibration head are fitted using validation data only, require no serving-time language-model inference, and keep each expert contribution separately inspectable.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'s_{\\text{fused}}(u,i)': 'Combined recommendation score for user u and item i', 'w_e(u)': 'Expert-specific weight for user u, summing to 1', 's_e(u,i)': 'Score produced by expert e'}
primitives.assumptions: Independent expert performance, disjoint information content, linear additivity of expert signals
primitives.breakdown_regime: Expert disagreement leading to score cancellation or amplification

layer2.mapping: Maps to conformal prediction combination in GSI; maps to multi-agent value function aggregation in GSE
layer2.telemetry: Average expert agreement rate and variance in fused scores

primitives.name: Bounded History Calibration
primitives.verbatim_quote: The fusion gate and calibration head are fitted using validation data only, require no serving-time language-model inference, and keep each expert contribution separately inspectable.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'s_{\\text{calibrated}}(u,i)': 'History-calibrated score', '\\lambda(u)': 'Per-user penalty strength, learned from validation', '\\mathbb{I}_{i \\in H_u}': "Indicator function for items in user u's history"}
primitives.assumptions: History items are known, penalty is additive, and optimal λ balances precision and recall
primitives.breakdown_regime: Over-penalization causing excessive cold-start bias or under-penalization leading to repetitive recommendations

layer2.mapping: Maps to Bayesian updating with informative priors in GSI; maps to state-transition cost functions in GSE
layer2.telemetry: Drop-off in recommended novelty and diversity metrics

primitives.name: Factorial Isolation Ablation
primitives.verbatim_quote: A factorial isolation ablation further shows that three-expert fusion without history calibration consistently outperforms calibrated SASRec, ruling out bounded history calibration as the sole explanation for the recovery.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'\\Delta': 'Performance difference between calibrated sequential model and fusion baseline', 'f': 'Evaluation metric (e.g., R@10)'}
primitives.assumptions: Experimental control holds, no interaction effects between fusion and calibration, identical model capacity
primitives.breakdown_regime: Failure to reject null hypothesis indicating fusion's superiority over calibration alone

layer2.mapping: Maps to randomized controlled trials in GSI; maps to counterfactual policy evaluation in GSE
layer2.telemetry: Statistical significance of performance gap between fusion and calibration

primitives.name: Text Embedding Perturbation
primitives.verbatim_quote: Randomly permuting item-text embeddings across item IDs while preserving model capacity reduces R@10 by 13.6%– 17.5%, showing that the gains depend on genuine item-text correspondence rather than additional representation capacity alone.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'R@10^{\\text{permuted}}': 'Top-10 recommendation precision after embedding permutation', 'R@10^{\\text{original}}': 'Original recommendation precision', '\\delta': 'relative drop in performance due to disrupted semantic correspondence'}
primitives.assumptions: Capacity held constant, semantic signal degraded while collaborative signal unchanged, IID perturbation
primitives.breakdown_regime: Complete shuffling eliminating all semantic correspondence, reverting to pure collaborative filtering ceiling

layer2.mapping: Maps to knockoff filter testing in GSI; maps to adversarial robustness assessment in GSE
layer2.telemetry: Correlation decay between original and permuted embeddings

It demonstrates that substantial improvements stem from leveraging pre-existing item-text correspondences rather than novel reasoning or heavy semantic machinery. The key insight is that recovery via simple, separately interpretable components often explains most of the observed lift, questioning the necessity of deploying opaque, high-complexity semantic systems without first establishing baseline performance from structured offline data.
